line: Same question, opposite answers. Confucius urged the slow student forward and kept the eager one back.
Sometimes the best horse may be the worst horse, and the worst horse can be the best one.
credit: Shunryu Suzuki · Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970)

line: Tsiolkovsky, nearly deaf from a childhood fever, left school and taught himself. Today he is called the father of astronautics.
credit: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky · Space Hall of Fame, 1976

line: The Buddha saw people like lotuses: some flourish under the water, some stand level, some rise above it.
credit: The Buddha, Samyutta Nikaya 6.1 · tr. Thanissaro Bhikkhu (adapted)

line: Feynman counted by talking to himself. John Tukey counted by picturing numbers. Same task, different minds.
credit: Richard Feynman · What Do You Care…, 1988

line: Not too gentle, not too hard: you can get it in your hand and feel it in your mind.
credit: Zhuangzi, ch. 13, the wheelwright · tr. Burton Watson

line: The world is going to need all of the different kinds of minds to work together.
If a man does not keep pace with his companions, perhaps it is because he hears a different drummer.
The essence of my father's teachings: the yoga practice must be tailored to fit each person.
credit: T.K.V. Desikachar on T. Krishnamacharya · The Heart of Yoga, 1995 (adapted)

line: What the child can do in cooperation today he can do alone tomorrow.
credit: Lev Vygotsky, Thought and Language, ch. 6 · tr. Hanfmann and Vakar
